"The direction of the electric field is determined by the motion of the positively charged particle. A positively charged particle moves in the direction of the electric field.
Deflection of particles:
Positive charge moves in the direction of the field.
Negative charge moves opposite to the direction of the field.
From your observation:
Particle 1 is positively charged and follows a parabolic path. This indicates that the electric field is directed upward (as the particle is deflected downward due to the force acting on it).
Particle 2 is negative and moves downward, meaning it is deflected opposite to the electric field (which is upward).
Particle 3 is positive and is deflected upward, indicating that the electric field is indeed directed upward.
Particle 4 is negative and is deflected downward, showing it moves opposite to the electric field.
Thus, the electric field is directed upward, and the deflections of particles 2, 3, and 4 are down, top, down respectively.
Answer: Option 1 — Top; down, top, down"

• Male is Rh- and female is Rh+: In this case, the mother is Rh-positive and the fetus can be either Rh-positive or Rh-negative. If the fetus is Rh-negative, there is no risk of Rh incompatibility
